maps.title: Madhurya Kadambini · Session 01 · Lack of True Knowledge

nodeData.note: · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Opening the Madhurya Kadambini festival, Maharaj names Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura's five causes of distress and takes up the first, avidya or lack of true knowledge. Everyone suffers from ignorance, and polished so-called knowledge is even more dangerous. The cure is real knowledge, which begins with humility, is received by approaching a bona fide guru and hearing like Pariksit and Arjuna, and is shown by acting on it. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note:
Maharaj presents Madhurya Kadambini as a book that both reveals the obstacles on the path and shows the solution. Like all acaryas, Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura's whole mood is how to help us, and his own life teaches as much as his books.

🎙 Maharaj at 04:26 (auto-transcript): “decided to come to this material to come and help us and as as we've seen from all other previous acharyas even to the present they have a particular in particular mood which they maintain throughout their entire life their main concern is how to help us Therefore, as the…”

An expert doctor diagnoses the disease, gives the medicine and also explains how to take it. Our spiritual doctors do the same, which is why Visvanatha lists the enemies that cause distress, so we can recognise them in ourselves. — “they also give a perfect prescription”

🎙 Maharaj at 06:30 (auto-transcript): “to us the the just like an expert doctor an expert physician knows how to diagnose the diseases of the patient who had come and not only that they also give a perfect prescription they give the medicine they give the medicine also give the prescription how to take the…”

Every conditioned soul is distressed, and even pure devotees face many troubles from us while trying to free us, as anyone treating a madman expects trouble. Still they are never disturbed, like actors who know their whole part before stepping on stage. — “They are like perfect dramatists who have perfectly realized”

🎙 Maharaj at 07:06 (auto-transcript): “practically, all conditional source, all living entities in this material are distressed, in one way or other. Even the pure devotees, even themselves, the pure devotees who come to this material, they have to face a lot of challenges. In the process of helping us to become…”

Maharaj lists Visvanatha's five causes of distress: avidya (lack of true knowledge), asmita (false ego), raga (attachment to material enjoyment), dvesa (envy) and abhinivesa (mundane absorption). The festival takes one each day, beginning with avidya.

🎙 Maharaj at 10:13 (auto-transcript): “What are the causes of distress? Vishwanachagravati, Takura listed them here. Abidya, Smita, Raga, Duesa, Bini, Visa, Pancha, Glesa. Abidya, nations for lack of true knowledge. Smita, Smita means false ego, false ego. Raga, attachment to material enjoyment. Envy, Dweisha, and…”

Ignorance is the root of sin and sin is the cause of all distress. Maharaj gives Srila Prabhupada's example of a person who commits a crime without knowing it and is still arrested and punished.

🎙 Maharaj at 11:40 (auto-transcript): “Nations or ignorance is the root of all sin. And sinful action is the cause of all distress. Slarupa Goswami explains all this in detail in his book, The Lecture of Devotion. that everyone suffers in this material world due to ignorance ignorance ignorance actually everyone…”

In the Bhagavatam's fourth canto Lord Siva says that of everything we cherish in this world, knowledge is the best. Maharaj concludes that everyone suffers because of ignorance; even those who misuse knowledge suffer from ignorance, never from true knowledge.

🎙 Maharaj at 13:03 (auto-transcript): “Here, Lord Shiva is encouraging us to repeat the song he has sung for Lord Krishna, singing the song sung by Lord Shiva. So in this chapter, Lord Shiva is explaining in this particular text, she was explaining that of all the things we cherish and appreciate in this material,…”

Anyone who really knows that fire burns will not put a finger in it. One who knows cannot act foolishly, so repeating sinful acts despite punishment shows we have not truly understood that sin brings suffering. — “If I really know that if I put my finger in a fire,”

🎙 Maharaj at 14:04 (auto-transcript): “No one who knows that if I put my finger in the fire, we burn, we put the finger there. No one can do it. If I really know that if I put my finger in a fire, it would be burned. I would not put my finger there. I had a friend who told me that if he sees money, if he sees…”

A friend once told Maharaj he would go for money even if a man sat beside it with a gun. Maharaj calls this ignorance: he does not understand why he lacks money and so takes a deadly risk to get it.

🎙 Maharaj at 14:23 (auto-transcript): “I had a friend who told me that if he sees money, if he sees money, not money, and someone is sitting there with a gun to shoot, he will go for the money. You can say that, yeah, this person knows that. The person is sitting there to kill whoever comes to take the money, but…”

children.topic: Why the pure devotee does not preach
children.note:
A leader of one religious group said that if everyone knew the results of sin, no one would need preaching. So in Satya-yuga no one preaches, and the uttama-bhakta does not preach because he sees no one in ignorance.

🎙 Maharaj at 15:43 (auto-transcript): “There is one religious organization. So their teaching is that complementing what the scripture is saying. He said, the leader of this organization said, that if every one of us knows the result of our sinful activities, no one will wait to be preached to. That is why in…”

The verse warns that both those who cultivate ignorance and those who cultivate a false, polished knowledge go into darkness, the latter even deeper. Maharaj asks why pious and educated people also suffer, and this is his answer.

Forgetting that the Lord owns everything is ignorance. A simple foolish person can change on meeting someone who knows, but so-called educationists think they know everything and lead others, so they are more dangerous.

🎙 Maharaj at 18:44 (auto-transcript): “The Supreme Lord is a proprietor of everything. And that forgetfulness of this fact is ignorance. The more a man forgets this fact of life, the more he is in darkness. In view of this, a godless civilization directed towards a so-called advancement of education is more…”

Maharaj asks us to imagine someone who has never driven taking the car keys, or a non-swimmer jumping into a big river. Ignorance is that dangerous: it keeps us bound to the reactions of our sins.

🎙 Maharaj at 20:01 (auto-transcript): “therefore they are more dangerous than those who are just ignorant ignorant can you imagine can you imagine a person who does not know how to drive you don't know how to drive you have no experience of driving can you imagine what will happen when he take the key and enter…”

The cure for avidya is its opposite, proper knowledge. Of all achievements true knowledge is highest, because no swimmer, however expert, can cross the ocean; only the boat of knowledge frees us from the anxieties of material life.

🎙 Maharaj at 21:31 (auto-transcript): “avidya. Next. What is the process of getting free from the distress due to avidya? Freedom from distress due to avidya. The opposite of proper knowledge and understanding casts out our distress. When we have proper knowledge, automatically, distress will be destroyed. So the…”

Lord Siva, Visvanatha Cakravarti, Rupa Goswami and Srila Prabhupada all say the same thing, because they share one mission, know the same disease and aim at the same goal. — “all other Acharyas agree with everything because they are one”

🎙 Maharaj at 23:38 (auto-transcript): “ignorance, Hamidya. So Lusiva explained this thing in detail, complementing or supporting what Vishnu Chakravati is, or Vishnu Chakravati is, complementing what Lusiva said, and all of Acharya, they have the same mission because they have the same goal and they know the same…”
These Gita verses list the qualities that make up knowledge, beginning with humility. Maharaj uses Srila Prabhupada's image of a staircase: many people stop on the first, second or third floor.

children.topic: Krishna the owner is the top floor
children.note:
Yoga, sankhya and other paths are lower floors. Complete knowledge, which fully removes ignorance, is understanding that Krishna is the supreme proprietor, controller and enjoyer of everything.

🎙 Maharaj at 25:31 (auto-transcript): “words, there are different processes of civil realization. Yoga is one of the means. Yoga, one of the means that many people try to follow varieties of yoga systems and people try to follow other people also follow another process the sankhya metaphysics and the other process…”

A person with knowledge naturally becomes humble, and detachment follows. Without Krishna consciousness our detachment is also avidya: history has many renunciants who fell and returned to what they had given up. — “one who has knowledge will naturally be humble”

🎙 Maharaj at 27:19 (auto-transcript): “One is considered to be knowledgeable. One is considered to be knowledgeable when one is exhibiting the qualities of one who has knowledge. One of the qualities Christians begin from in the Bhagavad Gita is humility. Humility. one who has knowledge will naturally be humble…”

Having shown the cause, Visvanatha now gives the way out: one must approach a bona fide spiritual master with humility, submission and service, and then true knowledge is revealed.

🎙 Maharaj at 29:19 (auto-transcript): “one must approach a bona fide spiritual massai in order to understand the transcendental missive to divide us the process of getting the knowledge it's a process so this natural gravity has already established for us the causes of our distress now he's giving the process of…”

Even a doctor who falls sick goes to another doctor. A distressed, bewildered person cannot help himself; he must go to someone peaceful and free from distress. Maharaj says this is compulsory.

🎙 Maharaj at 29:48 (auto-transcript): “a bona fide spiritual master just like a person who is sick the person who is sick even if you are a doctor you cannot treat yourself you have to go to another doctor in the same way a distressful person means one is bewildered and confused you cannot help yourself you have…”

children.topic: Go to the sadhu with ears
children.note:
Krishna consciousness begins with hearing, sravana. We should not visit the sadhu just to see him, but to hear, because he pours the medicine for avidya in through the ears. Prabhupada asked people simply to come, sit down and hear. — “We should go with the ear.”

🎙 Maharaj at 30:50 (auto-transcript): “be revealed to us. The beginning of Krishna consciousness and devotional service is hearing. The Sanskrit is called Slavana. When one leans his ears to give oral reception to the transdental vibrations, he can quickly become purified and cleansed in the heart. This is what…”

Pariksit had faith in Sukadeva Goswami and was convinced he could cure his disease. As a full belly shows we have eaten, destroyed ignorance is the proof that we have really heard.

🎙 Maharaj at 32:40 (auto-transcript): “Next, how to do sravana. like Parishit Maharaj. Hearing has qualification, has qualities. So here, this qualification, what's the qualification of Parishit Maharaj to hear from Sukhadev Goswami? What's the qualification? the qualification that one should go with the ear and…”

Pariksit had literally seven days to live. Ours are relative, maybe ten or fifty years, but we too must leave the body, so we should hear with his urgency, and then a miracle happens: he felt Krishna planted in his heart and his fear was gone.

🎙 Maharaj at 34:27 (auto-transcript): “What is Parashit Mahara's situation? His situation is that he has only, he's in emergency, he's in emergency world, emergency world. He has only seven days to live the body. Every one of us in this matter will have seven days. Our seven days is relative, relative. Someone's…”
In this verse Arjuna tells Krishna his illusion is gone and he is ready to act. Maharaj says the proof that the disease is cured is this readiness to act as the Lord desires.

Maharaj answers devotees' questions on living the knowledge, hearing, and measuring progress.

🎙 Maharaj at 41:16 (auto-transcript): “i think that who has raised his hand yes maroon can you hear me yes okay um sorry you might have covered maybe i might have ignored it i'm sorry for that uh so regarding the point you know we not knowing uh krishna is the proprietor of everything is a mode of ignorance uh at…”

A devotee is convinced Krishna is the proprietor but still feels 'it is mine' in daily life.

🎙 Question from the floor at 41:16 (auto-transcript): “i think that who has raised his hand yes maroon can you hear me yes okay um sorry you might have covered maybe i might have ignored it i'm sorry for that uh so regarding the point you know we not knowing uh krishna is the proprietor of everything is a mode of ignorance uh at…”

Knowing in theory but not in action is still ignorance; the speculators in scripture are the jnanis, not the karmis. Saying 'I am not this body' becomes real knowledge only when we act as a soul.

🎙 Maharaj at 42:07 (auto-transcript): “i do in the in my life so how can i implement that the the fact that we still theoretically understand christian is the proprietor but in action in actuality we don't do that that that is a video it means we have not known yet that christian is a supreme proprietor…”

We already offer food to Krishna and pray, but often unconsciously. Now we should do it consciously, offering everything first, using our salary or profit in His service and asking His permission, until it becomes our own experience. — “But now we have to do it consciously.”

🎙 Maharaj at 44:03 (auto-transcript): “Now we shall start to practice acting, acting that yes, Krishna is a proprietor of everything. And Prabhupada has given us the practical way to do it. We are doing it imperceptibly, Avidya. We are doing it imperceptibly. We are doing it unconsciously. We are doing it. But now…”

A disciple asks how hearing with the ears fits with the advice to filter what we hear.

🎙 Question from the floor at 48:04 (auto-transcript): “Hare Krishna Gurudev, please accept my frustrated obeisances. Thank you very, very much Gurudev for the wonderful class. I am extremely delighted. Gurudev, in the context of the class, you said that when we go to meet a sadhu, we should not go to meet the sadhu with just our…”

The sadhu did not call us; we went to him, as a patient takes himself to the hospital. Doubting his medicine is our avidya, and our filtering is only as good as our understanding, so we follow scientifically and become purified. — “A doctor never comes to my house”

🎙 Maharaj at 49:07 (auto-transcript): “For us to go to sadhu for the years, why do we have to do that? The sadhu didn't call for us. It is we who have gone to meet him or meet her. It is we who have gone. A doctor never comes to my house and says, oh my friend, you are sick, come to my hospital. No doctor does…”

children.topic: Q3 · No intense desire to hear
children.note:
Maharaj says to keep pushing ourselves to hear even when tired; going to hear is a sacrifice, and by continuing, one day we will really hear and start acting on it. — “we should continue to push ourselves to hear”

🎙 Question from the floor at 51:02 (auto-transcript): “We have, our next question is from Paramgati Prabhuji. He's asking, we hear and like to hear, but still don't have that intense desire to hear. Like you mentioned, Parikshit Maharaj has. What can be done to improve our situation? we should continue to push ourselves to hear…”

A devotee asks how to measure where they are among the stages of devotional service.

🎙 Question from the floor at 52:40 (auto-transcript): “from uh one vihari prabhuji he's saying harry krishna our dear beloved gurudev please kindly accept our most humble obeisances we thank you very much for your wonderful lectures Please kindly enlighten us how we can measure at what stage we are in the nine stages of…”

As a mirror shows the face, scripture shows a sincere devotee his stage: eagerness to hear, taste in chanting and devotee association, and determination to face challenges instead of constant complaining. — “Just like if we take a mirror before our face”

🎙 Maharaj at 53:07 (auto-transcript): “Where we are in our Christian consciousness is not difficult to understand. Just like if we take a mirror before our face, we'll see where that impulse is on our face. We'll see if we are racist on our face. We will see whatever is happening on our face. We'll see. Or like if…”

Another measure is whether we try to look purest or instead encourage every devotee we meet. Krishna and pure bhakti are unlimited, but our practice is measurable, and we should measure it.

🎙 Maharaj at 55:18 (auto-transcript): “But we will know that we are developing knowledge and we'll start seeing how we are making advancement for the stage where we are in our Christian consciousness by how do I relate with my brothers and sisters. and my relationship is to show how i'm the purest among all or is…”

Further answers on attention in class, humility, discussing obstacles, and knowing yet still being attracted.

🎙 Maharaj at 57:12 (auto-transcript): “Maharaj and our next question is from Avesh Rupar Prabhuji. He is asking, Hari Krishna Dilar Shirov Gurudev, thank you so much for this wonderful class. My question is that we are sitting in the class but we are not hearing actually. Instead we are spaced out. So how do we…”

We do not hear because we feel comfortable: young body, family well, business growing, dreams of position and disciples. Then the mind gives its own class. Arjuna and Pariksit were distressed and gave full attention, so we should not feel comfortable here. — “We are not hearing because we are still feeling comfortable with our material life.”

🎙 Question from the floor at 57:12 (auto-transcript): “Maharaj and our next question is from Avesh Rupar Prabhuji. He is asking, Hari Krishna Dilar Shirov Gurudev, thank you so much for this wonderful class. My question is that we are sitting in the class but we are not hearing actually. Instead we are spaced out. So how do we…”

A devotee asks what true humility looks like.

🎙 Question from the floor at 61:00 (auto-transcript): “Thank you so much, Maharaj. So beautifully you have described this. We have one more question from Facebook by Murari Mohandas Prabhuji, he's saying, Dhanwath Maharaj, I have heard that humility is like a trade secret. Could you give an example of true humility? What does it…”

True humility is not being eager for respect, reward or honour. Maharaj knows devotees who left because they felt unappreciated after serving through war and pandemic; that is avidya and lack of humility.

🎙 Maharaj at 61:21 (auto-transcript): “True humility, as the Prophet explained, means that we should not be eager to get the respect from others. We should not be eager to get the reward. Yes. I have done so much and I should be appreciated. I know so many devotees left this movement because they felt not…”

Telling people the truth makes them dislike you, yet we say it only to help, caring for the soul. So Prabhupada calling us rascals is humility, like a healer in Maharaj's village whose hand no one may hold while he works. — “true humility means we are ready to become unpopular.”

🎙 Maharaj at 62:31 (auto-transcript): “And so the Baptist said, true humility means we are ready to become unpopular. how is that because if you tell the truth if you tell the truth your people if you say the truth to the people they will not like you that is true humility that i i am not i i'm not saying it to…”

Yes; no one wants distress and we do not know how to be free, so the acaryas take pains to show us. Otherwise it would not be discussed.

🎙 Question from the floor at 66:11 (auto-transcript): “And now our next question is from Aditya Prabhu. Hare Krishna Srila Gurudev, please accept my humble obeisances. Maharaj, revealing obstacles in our practice, is it always necessary? Yes, it is necessary. If it's not necessary, we don't waste our time to speak about it. It is…”

children.note:
Maharaj says that being drawn to the fire shows we do not really know. As eating fills the belly, real knowing ends foolishness; pure devotees do not suffer in hard situations because of their knowledge. — “If you have eaten, your belly will be full.”

nodeData.note: · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Maharaj takes up asmita, false ego, the second of Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura's five causes of distress: accepting the body as the self, which breeds selfishness, anger and offences and blocks the humility needed to accept discipline. He measures advancement by freedom from false ego and gives tools to reduce it: Guru and Krishna consciousness, following Krishna's plan, spiritual alertness, selflessness without self-pity, and prayer. In questions he speaks on serving superiors, accepting correction, kinds of humility, real ego, and the danger of judging by appearance. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.topic: Asmita, the second cause of distress
children.note:
Following Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura's five causes of distress, Maharaj moves from yesterday's avidya (ignorance) to asmita, false ego. He explains that ahankara and asmita mean the same, yet differ slightly: ahankara is an element of material energy, while asmita is its symptom showing in our behaviour. — “when you have two things, there's always some difference.”

🎙 Maharaj at 12:01 (auto-transcript): “Dr. Grishuno Chakravati Chakravati, as we were discussing yesterday, gave us five causes of distress. So yesterday we looked at Abidya, nations. A lack of true knowledge brings distress. So today, this morning, we are going to look at Asmita, false signal. Most of us are…”

False ego is accepting the body as oneself, and at root it is selfishness. Because something is called false, there must be an original: the real ego is the soul as Krishna's eternal servant, which never changes.

🎙 Maharaj at 13:33 (auto-transcript): “So, understanding false ego. What is false ego? False ego means accepting this body as oneself. When one understands that he is not distant to his body and his spirit soul, he comes to his real ego. Ego is there. False ego is condemned, but not real ego. If you have something…”

False ego changes because it is material and time acts on everything material; the real ego is untouched by time. When real knowledge comes, the bodily identification and the distress it causes are destroyed.

🎙 Maharaj at 14:33 (auto-transcript): “But false ego can change because it is material. All material thing changes in course of time. The time affects everything material, but time does not affect anything spiritual. So the real ego does not change, but false ego changed from time to time. That means now I am…”

Anyone who becomes angry is acting from false ego, as if saying, 'Why did you step on my foot, don't you know who I am?' An insult leads to a slap, a fight, money spent, the police and even death.

🎙 Maharaj at 16:42 (auto-transcript): “And it means selfishness, selfishness, selfish, selfish. That we get angry. That we won't get angry in this material. It means what? False ego. One who has no false ego would not be angry at anything, at anyone. That anyone, anyone who gets angry is affected by false ego, is…”

children.topic: My face is ugly, not me
children.note:
If someone mocks his ugly face, Maharaj says the face may be ugly but the soul is not, since it is not material. Taking the body as self makes us react to whatever happens to it. — “My face is ugly, but I'm not ugly.”

🎙 Maharaj at 17:34 (auto-transcript): “Or somebody insults you. Look at the other. Look at my ugly face. My face is ugly, but I'm not ugly. Because the spirit surely is not ugly. The spirit surely is not material. Therefore, it's beautiful. But due to a false ego, I'm accepting that this body, which is material,…”

Maharaj repeats that false ego is the central interference in spiritual life. The falsely proud lack the humility to accept discipline, so they resist even the arrangements Krishna and the guru make for their purification.

🎙 Maharaj at 19:08 (auto-transcript): “Because this false ego causes misery. We should look at it as an obstacle. It's a major obstacle, major obstacle is confronting every conditional source socially mentally and even intellectually we may be able to fool others and ourselves but when it comes to false ego we…”

Citing a book called Surrender, Maharaj says that to become humble we need humiliation, but false ego refuses to accept it as too much to bear. — “For anyone to become very humble, we need humiliation.”

🎙 Maharaj at 21:17 (auto-transcript): “the process, due to false sigil. For anyone to, he solidized Bhakti Chamarai to explain all these things in his book Surrender. For anyone to become very humble, we need humiliation. Well, false sigil would not allow humiliation to take place. We would not accept humiliation.…”

children.topic: Who are you to instruct me?
children.note:
Many devotees feel superior to their spiritual master. Maharaj recalls a godbrother, older in age than their guru, who found it a lifelong struggle to accept his instruction.

🎙 Maharaj at 22:02 (auto-transcript): “Asmita, false ego. Who are you to instruct me? Who are you to instruct me? Who are you to talk to me like this? Who are you that I should bow down, I should respect, I should offer my head to? Who are you? Many many devotees. There are many devotees who feel that they are…”
These Gita verses list the items of knowledge, beginning with humility. Even a worldly teacher says, 'Bend down low, then I will teach you.' — “Without humility, we cannot learn.”

We are called disciples because we are to be disciplined by the spiritual master, and false ego blocks that; this is why many cannot continue in Krishna consciousness.

🎙 Maharaj at 25:32 (auto-transcript): “we are called disciples. Why? Because we have to be disciplined by spiritual master. We have to be disciplined. To become a disciple, we have to be disciplined. A false ego would be an obstruction for us to accept discipline. False ego. So many people cannot make it in…”

Quoting the Bhagavatam, Maharaj calls false ego the chain of material existence: thinking ourselves the enjoyers, every species struggles hard to gratify the body. Srila Prabhupada says such hard struggle is not life or enjoyment but punishment.

🎙 Maharaj at 26:27 (auto-transcript): “Binding force. We all know what is binding. All of us who have experience of binding, when one is chained, when one is chained, So the shackle of falsehood binds all conditions or the material world to think that I am a supreme enjoyer and I have to enjoy this body. So look…”

From the Bible, Maharaj recalls that after Cain killed Abel he was cursed to till the ground and sweat for his maintenance, which he traces to false ego.

🎙 Maharaj at 27:28 (auto-transcript): “In the Bible, it was said that when Cain killed his brother, Abel, God cursed him. You will till the ground. You will till the ground. You will suffer seriously and sweat before you get what you need to maintain yourself. Why? False ego. False ego. It's a binding force. So…”

The more we think of ourselves and try to push Krishna from the centre, the more we fuel the fire of false ego. Gloom and anxiety follow, and our enthusiasm burns away with our devotional credits.

🎙 Maharaj at 28:27 (auto-transcript): “The more that we just think of ourselves, selfishness, we started from selfishness, false ego, selfishness. The more we are simply thinking of ourselves, putting ourselves in the center, and trying to remove Krishna from the center, false ego, the more we are supporting or…”

False ego makes it very easy to step on others' toes, and we do it constantly. We chant for a moment, then false ego covers it up for the rest of the day.

🎙 Maharaj at 29:07 (auto-transcript): “false ego we can never we can never avoid to make offense it is very very easy for us to step on so many people's tools but false ego very very easy in fact it's the easiest thing it's the easiest thing is the easiest way for us to offend anyone to make offense false ego A…”

Asked how one knows one is advancing, Maharaj gives a measure: how far one is free of false ego, seen in how much humiliation one can accept and how firmly one knows, 'I am constitutionally a servant; Krishna is the master.'

🎙 Maharaj at 31:17 (auto-transcript): “Spiritual technology is to be free from falsehood, as meta, falsehood, a technology, the tool, the tool for us to be free from falsehood. What is that? Advancement is measured by the degree to which we are devoid of falsehood. We want to know one of the questions, what are…”

children.topic: Be conscious of Guru and Krishna
children.note:

nodeData.note: BG 2.62; SB 3.25.20 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Maharaj explains raga, material attachment, as the third cause of distress: it grows from dwelling on sense objects, blocks our hearing in devotional life and leaves even the wealthiest empty. Since attachment can never be killed, only transferred, he gives four remedies: prioritise the eternal, refuse distractions, dovetail everything in Krishna's service and cultivate attachment to Sri Guru. In the questions he explains how money, eating and association can either bind us or carry us to Krishna. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

Maharaj takes up dvesa, envy, the fourth cause of distress in Madhurya Kadambini: being unhappy at another's glory, a self-centred attack that destroys intelligence, as with Citraketu's co-wives. children.note:
Maharaj continues Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura's five causes of distress. After avidya, asmita and raga, and after a Mataji's talk the day before on the defeatist mentality, today's subject is dvesa, envy. The Thakura came from Goloka not to struggle like us but to warn us of obstacles and show, step by step, how to fall madly in love with Krishna.

children.topic: Bothered or not, it is envy

'I deserve this, I am better than him' is the self-centred mood that draws envy in. The more we think only of ourselves the more we suffer, and the conflict we carry inside spills onto everyone around us. An envious person expects bad things for the other and cannot even hear him truthfully.

nodeData.note: · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Maharaj explains abhinivesa, the fifth cause of distress: absorption in the body and in sense gratification as the goal of life, which blinds us to self-realization and blocks spiritual practice. He warns that we cannot cheat Krishna and gives three remedies: stop sin at the planning stage, live regulated and clean, and observe fasting days while keeping devotee association. Questions follow on choosing association, hurtful devotees, work parties, a disturbed mind and using free time. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note:
Maharaj recalls the four causes already covered — ignorance, false ego, attachment and envy — and introduces the fifth, abhinivesa or mundane engagement. He adds the trap a devotee spoke of the day before: feeling like a failure and thinking oneself incapable.

Pure devotees know they are incapable on their own yet live joyfully, because there is a way to become capable.
